pointers.sentence: The setting's default is `ModelBackend` alone (`django/conf/global_settings.py`).
`django.contrib.auth.load_backend` imports the class a dotted path names and calls it, so each call makes a new instance (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:load_backend`).
`get_backends` does that for every path of the setting, and raises `ImproperlyConfigured` when there is none (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:_get_backends`).
`authenticate` takes the request, `None` unless given, and the credentials as keyword arguments (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:authenticate`).

It passes over every backend that cannot take them: `_get_compatible_backends`, a generator, reads each backend's authenticate method with `signature` as the loop reaches it and binds the request and the credentials to it, and a `TypeError` skips the backend ([Asking a callable what it accepts: `django/utils/inspect.py`](../utils/inspect.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:_get_compatible_backends`).

It passes over every backend that cannot take them: `_get_compatible_backends`, a generator, reads each backend's authenticate method with `signature` as the loop reaches it and binds the request and the credentials to it, and a `TypeError` skips the backend ([Asking a callable what it accepts: `django/utils/inspect.py`](../utils/inspect.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:_get_compatible_backends`).

The sender is the module's name, `"django.contrib.auth"`; the receiver gets the request, and the credentials with `_clean_credentials` having masked the value of every key containing api, token, key, secret, password or signature, a list its docstring calls not comprehensive (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:_clean_credentials`).

`aauthenticate` is the same loop, awaiting each backend's `BaseBackend.aauthenticate` and sending the signal with `Signal.asend`; it picks the backends by their synchronous method's signature (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:aauthenticate`).

Every method `BaseBackend` declares answers no: `BaseBackend.authenticate` and `BaseBackend.get_user` return `None`, `BaseBackend.get_user_permissions` and `BaseBackend.get_group_permissions` an empty set, and `BaseBackend.has_perm` looks in those two (`django/contrib/auth/backends.py:BaseBackend`).

`ModelBackend.authenticate` takes username and password, or, for the username, the keyword argument named after the user model's `USERNAME_FIELD`; without both it returns `None` (`django/contrib/auth/backends.py:ModelBackend.authenticate`).

Given none, it sets the password on an unsaved instance of the user model, which runs the default hasher once for nothing; its docstring's reason is to prevent user enumeration attacks, ticket 20760 (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:check_password_with_timing_attack_mitigation`).
`ModelBackend.get_user` applies the same test, so a user made inactive is not found at the next request of a session (`django/contrib/auth/backends.py:ModelBackend.get_user`).

Apache's mod_wsgi can call Django's `check_password` outside the request cycle (`docs/howto/deployment/wsgi/apache-auth.txt`): `None` when no active user has the name, otherwise whether the password matches, by the same timing function and without the backends (`django/contrib/auth/handlers/modwsgi.py:check_password`).

When the web server has authenticated the browser, Django has only to believe the name it passes on (`docs/howto/auth-remote-user.txt`).

`RemoteUserBackend.configure_user`, given the user and whether it was just created, returns it unchanged unless overridden; the inherited `user_can_authenticate` refuses an inactive user (`django/contrib/auth/backends.py:RemoteUserBackend.authenticate`).

It serves either kind of chain, running `RemoteUserMiddleware.process_request`, or in an asynchronous one `RemoteUserMiddleware.aprocess_request`, before the layer inside, and does nothing on the way out (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:RemoteUserMiddleware`).

Under ASGI there is no environ, and `RemoteUserMiddleware.get_username` reads `"HTTP_REMOTE_USER"`, the Remote-User header, while `header` is the default; a subclass's `header` is read as written, as `"HTTP_AUTHUSER"` (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:RemoteUserMiddleware.get_username`).
The documentation's warning follows: under ASGI a reverse proxy must always set or strip the header (`docs/howto/auth-remote-user.txt`).
Under ASGI a custom `header` is again read without an added `"HTTP_"`, as before 5.2 (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
